title: Sore gum behind my last tooth

patient.name: Aisha Raza
patient.complaint: Pain and swelling at the back of my lower left jaw.
patient.opening: It's right at the back on the bottom left. The gum is swollen and it tastes horrible.

topics.label: When it started
topics.answer: Four days ago. It's happened once before, last year, but it went away.

topics.label: Bad taste or discharge
topics.answer: Yes, a horrible salty taste, and my breath smells.

topics.label: Mouth opening
topics.answer: It's hard to open wide, it feels stiff.

topics.label: Swallowing and breathing
topics.answer: Swallowing is a bit uncomfortable on that side, but I can eat and drink. Breathing is fine.

topics.label: Feeling unwell
topics.answer: No fever. I think there's a tender lump under my jaw.

topics.label: Biting
topics.answer: When I close, the top tooth seems to bite on the swollen gum.

topics.label: Medical history
topics.answer: I take the contraceptive pill. No allergies.

topics.label: Where exactly
topics.answer: Right at the very back, behind my last tooth on the bottom left.

items.question: Click the tooth at the centre of the problem.
items.helper: Look right at the back of the lower left.
items.explain: The partly erupted lower left third molar (38), covered by an inflamed flap of gum (the operculum).
items.reveal: 38 is partly erupted. The operculum over it is red and swollen with pus underneath. 28 bites on the flap. Mouth opening is 28 mm.

items.question: What would you check or arrange? Select all that apply.
items.explain: Mouth opening and systemic signs tell you how severe and how far spread it is; an OPG shows the position of 38 and decay on 37.

findings.Temperature and neck lymph nodes: 37.2 °C. One tender submandibular lymph node on the left.
findings.OPG: 38 is mesioangularly impacted against 37. No caries on 37.
findings.Blood tests: Not needed; she is systemically well.

items.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.explain: Inflammation of the gum flap around a partly erupted third molar, with pus, a bad taste and limited opening, is pericoronitis.

items.question: In one or two sentences, justify your diagnosis.
items.expected: A partly erupted, impacted 38 with a swollen, inflamed operculum and pus, a bad taste, trismus and an upper tooth biting on the flap.

items.question: What is the best management today?
options: Irrigate under the flap, pain relief and warm salt rinses; review
answer: Irrigate under the flap, pain relief and warm salt rinses; review
items.explain: Local measures come first. Antibiotics are for spreading infection or a systemically unwell patient. Removing 38 is considered once it has settled, especially as this is a repeat episode.

items.question: When should Aisha seek urgent help?
items.expected: If she struggles to swallow or breathe, if the swelling spreads into the neck or face, if she develops a fever or feels very unwell, or if she can barely open her mouth.

teachingPoints: Pericoronitis is inflammation of the operculum over a partly erupted tooth, most often a lower third molar.
Local measures first; antibiotics only for spreading infection or systemic signs.
Difficulty swallowing or breathing is an emergency.
